messages.content: I'm a freelance illustrator called Aisha. Write a polite message to a client asking for payment of an overdue invoice, about 70 words.

Dear Mr. Kapoor,
I hope you are doing well. This is a gentle reminder that the invoice for the book cover illustrations, sent on 3rd March, is now two weeks overdue. I have attached a copy for your reference. I would be grateful if you could arrange the payment this week. Please tell me if there is any problem with the invoice.
Thank you,
Aisha
Write a tiny story of about 90 words about an old tree that is going to be cut down, and the children who save it.

The old neem tree at the end of Station Road had given shade for sixty years. One Monday, a notice appeared on its trunk: it would be cut down to widen the road. The children of the lane were shocked. That evening, they made posters, collected signatures from every house and met the ward officer with their parents. They explained how birds nested in it and how vendors rested beneath it. A week later, a new notice appeared. The road would curve gently around the tree instead. The children held a picnic under it to celebrate.
Please write a paragraph, about 90 words, about why I love collecting stamps. I'm 12.

I started collecting stamps when my uncle gave me an old album he had kept since college. At first I just liked the bright colours, but soon I began to notice the stories behind them. One stamp shows a tiger from the Sundarbans, and another shows a sailing ship from a country I had never heard of. Each one makes me curious, so I look it up in the atlas. Now I have more than three hundred stamps. My dream is to find one from every country in the world.
I need a sorry note for my friend Zara. I cancelled our plans at the last minute twice this month. Under 60 words.

Zara, I'm really sorry for cancelling on you twice this month, especially at the last minute. That wasn't fair to you, and I know you had made time for me. You deserve better than that. Let me make it up to you: you pick the day and the place, and I promise I'll be there.
Could you write a thank-you card from my parents to my uncle, who helped us move house? Around 60 words.

Dear Ravi,
Thank you so much for all your help with our move. We could not have done it without you. You packed boxes, carried heavy furniture and even fixed the fan in the new kitchen. Most of all, your jokes kept everyone smiling on a very tiring day. Please come for dinner soon.
With love and thanks,
Mohan and Geeta
I just finished my first pottery class. Write a short post for my personal blog about it, about 90 words.

Today I sat at a pottery wheel for the first time, and it was much harder than it looks. The clay kept wobbling and collapsing, and within minutes my hands and face were covered in mud. Our teacher, Mrs. Kulkarni, kept saying, "Slow down. Let the wheel do the work." By the end of the class, I had made one small, crooked bowl. It leans to one side and has a thumbprint on the rim, but I have never been prouder of anything. Next week, I'm trying a cup.
Write a notice, about 60 words, for the school notice board announcing an inter-house quiz competition.

NOTICE: Inter-House Quiz Competition
An inter-house quiz will be held on Friday, 12 July, at 11 am in the school auditorium. Each house must send a team of three students from Classes 8 to 10. Topics include science, history, sports and general knowledge. Names must be given to the house captains by Tuesday. Come and cheer for your house!
- Quiz Club
Write a short paragraph, under 80 words, explaining to a 7-year-old why we can't buy every toy we see.

Money is a bit like the water in your bottle. There is only so much of it, so we have to choose carefully how to use it. Mummy and Papa need money for food, school, the house and many other things. If we buy every toy we see, there won't be enough left for important things. But if we wait and choose one special toy, we can enjoy it even more.
I'd like a short story, about 100 words, about a family stuck at home during a thunderstorm when the lights go out.

The thunder cracked so loudly that the windows rattled, and then the lights went out. Little Arya screamed and grabbed her father's arm. "Nobody panic," said Papa, who was clearly panicking as he searched for the torch. Ma found a candle instead. The family gathered in the living room, and Dadi began telling the story of the night a storm blew the roof off her father's cowshed. Soon everyone was laughing at her funny voices. Rain drummed on the roof, but nobody noticed anymore. When the lights came back, Arya groaned. "Can we switch them off again?"
Draft a message to a job recruiter thanking her for yesterday's interview. About 70 words. I'm Rohit Malhotra, and I interviewed for a data analyst role.

Dear Ms. Sen,
Thank you for taking the time to interview me yesterday for the Data Analyst position. I enjoyed learning more about your team and the projects you are working on. Our conversation about the customer survey data made me even more excited about the role. I would be happy to share any further information you may need.
Best regards,
Rohit Malhotra
Describe a plate of steaming momos on a cold evening, roughly 60 words, for a food blog.

There is nothing quite like a plate of steaming momos on a cold evening. The thin, soft wrappers are pleated by hand and puffed up from the steam. When you bite into one, hot juice spills out, so you have to be careful. Dip it in the fiery red chutney, and suddenly the cold outside does not matter at all.
Write a 90-word description of a forest walk in the early morning, using the senses.

The forest is cool and quiet when I step onto the narrow path. Sunlight falls through the leaves in thin golden lines. Under my shoes, dry twigs snap and damp earth gives softly. The air smells of moss, wet bark and some sweet, hidden flower. Somewhere above, a woodpecker taps steadily, and a pair of bulbuls call to each other. I touch the rough trunk of an old teak tree and feel the morning dew on my fingers. With every step, the noise of the world seems further away.
Write a message, about 70 words, to my housing society suggesting we start composting our kitchen waste.

Dear neighbours,
Every day, our society sends a lot of vegetable peels and food waste to the landfill. I'd like to suggest that we start composting it instead. A compost bin near the garden would turn our kitchen waste into rich soil for our plants within a few months. It costs very little and would reduce our garbage. If you're interested, please join a short meeting in the clubhouse on Sunday at 6 pm.
Rahul Desai, B-302
Make up a short bedtime story, about 100 words, about a teddy bear who is afraid of the dark.

Every night, when the lights went off, Bhalu the teddy bear trembled on the shelf. The dark made the cupboard look like a giant and the curtains look like ghosts. One night, little Kiaan heard a tiny sniff. He climbed out of bed, took Bhalu down and hugged him. "The dark is just the day sleeping," Kiaan whispered. "Everything is still here." He showed Bhalu the moon outside the window and the night light shaped like a star. Bhalu stopped trembling. From then on, he slept tucked under Kiaan's arm, and neither of them was afraid anymore.
Write the opening lines, about 50 words, of a welcome speech for our school's annual day, to be given by the head girl.

Good evening, respected Chief Guest, our Principal, teachers, parents and dear friends. On behalf of the students of Green Valley School, I warmly welcome you to our twenty-fifth Annual Day. Tonight, our stage will come alive with music, dance and drama that we have prepared with great love. Thank you for being here.
Our colleague Rekha lost her mother last week. Draft a sympathy card message from the team, about 50 words.

Dear Rekha,
We are deeply sorry for the loss of your mother. Please accept our heartfelt sympathy. We are holding you and your family in our thoughts during this difficult time. Take all the time you need, and know that we are here for you in any way that helps.
With love,
Your colleagues
Write a polite email, under 70 words, to my bank asking for a duplicate passbook because I lost mine.

Subject: Request for a duplicate passbook
Dear Sir or Madam,
I hold a savings account at your MG Road branch, with an account number ending in 4471. I have lost my passbook and would like to request a duplicate. Please tell me which documents I need to bring and whether any fee applies. I can visit the branch any weekday morning.
Thank you,
Lalit Arora
Help me invite all my building's neighbours to a small Ganesh Chaturthi aarti at my flat. About 60 words.

Dear neighbours,
We are bringing Ganpati Bappa home this Ganesh Chaturthi, and we would love for you to join us for the evening aarti. Please come to Flat 502 on Saturday at 7:30 pm. Prasad and modaks will be served afterwards. Children are especially welcome. Come as you are, and bring your voices for the aarti!
Warmly,
The Kulkarni family
For a teen magazine, write under 90 words about how it's okay not to be good at everything.

Nobody is good at everything, and nobody needs to be. You might be brilliant at drawing but hopeless at maths, or great at football but terrible at singing. That is completely normal. Every person has a different set of strengths. Trying new things is wonderful, even if you are bad at them, because the fun is in the learning. So be patient with yourself. Notice what you love and what you are getting better at. The rest can wait.
For descriptive writing class, describe a busy market in the evening in about 100 words.

By six in the evening, the market wakes up. Strings of yellow bulbs flicker on above the stalls, and the smell of frying pakoras drifts through the air. Vegetable sellers call out their prices over the honking of scooters squeezing through the narrow lane. A woman bargains firmly over a pile of shining brinjals, while her small son tugs at her sari, pointing at a balloon seller. Bangles clink at one stall, and pressure cookers stand stacked like towers at another. Everyone seems to be in a hurry, yet nobody really wants to leave.
